title: Reading Ollama response durations and token speeds
description: This example parses an Ollama chat response to compute input and output token throughput, showing that reading the prompt is fast and parallel while writing tokens is slow and sequential.

steps.description: The resp dictionary holds a real Ollama response from Model 4's step 1 plan phase. It includes total_duration, load_duration, prompt_eval_count, prompt_eval_duration, eval_count, and eval_duration, all in nanoseconds.
The key fields: 412 input tokens took 610ms (prompt_eval_duration), 41 output tokens took 2100ms (eval_duration), and the total was 2773ms. The load_duration of 12ms is negligible.
NS converts nanoseconds to seconds. in_tok and out_tok extract the token counts. read_s, write_s, and total_s convert the durations to seconds.
Three print statements show the throughput: input tokens at ~675 tokens/s, output tokens at ~19.5 tokens/s, and that writing took 76% of the total time.

steps.question: What does the trace line printed at the end contain?
steps.answer: It contains the trace_id, step, phase, the measured prompt_tokens and completion_tokens, the total latency in milliseconds, and the finish_reason from the response.

steps.description: The trace line is built from the measured numbers, not estimates. It records 412 prompt tokens, 41 completion tokens, 2773ms latency, and finish_reason stop.
The first print shows: 412 input tokens read in 0.61 seconds at 675 tokens per second.
The second print shows: 41 output tokens written in 2.10 seconds at 19.5 tokens per second.
The third print shows: total 2.77 seconds, writing was 76% of the time.
The trace line is printed with the measured token counts, latency, and finish_reason.
